Overview of endocrine system • “Glands” in human body can be divided into endocrine glands and exocrine glands. • Endocrine glands: ductless glands that secrete hormones into blood • Exocrine glands: glands that secrete nonhormone chemicals to a surface through ducts • Sweat gland, skin sebaceous gland, and gastric gland are examples of exocrine glands. • Only endocrine glands belong to “endocrine system”.

• Hormones are carried by blood to all tissues. However, not all cells are affected by 1 hormone.
• The cells, that are affected, are “target cells” of a certain hormone.
• These cells have specific receptor proteins in cytoplasm or in cell membrane.
• Hormone molecules bind to receptor proteins and trigger a series of changes of these cells.

• (3) Second messengers activate or inactivate enzymes inside cytoplasm.
• (4) Cellular activities are changed!

quotation_candidates.quotation: • The endocrine system and nervous system are two major parts of human’s coordinating system to integrate activities of all cells and responses to both internal and external changes.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • A cell (Endocrine gland cell) secretes a chemical.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • The chemical (Hormone) travel through the blood.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Another cell (Target cell) is stimulated to change activities.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Reproduction (E.g. estrogen and testosterone)

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Growth and development (E.g. growth hormone)

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Balance of ions, water, and nutrients (E.g. insulin)

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Regulation of cellular metabolism (E.g. epinephrine)

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Regulation of body defenses (E.g. Thymosin)

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • “Glands” in human body can be divided into endocrine glands and exocrine glands.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Endocrine glands: ductless glands that secrete hormones into blood

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Exocrine glands: glands that secrete nonhormone chemicals to a surface through ducts

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Sweat gland, skin sebaceous gland, and gastric gland are examples of exocrine glands.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Only endocrine glands belong to “endocrine system”.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Chemical structure of a hormone determines its solubility in water. This is related to:

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • How is it transported in blood?

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • How does it affect its target cells?

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (1) Protein or amino acid based Most hormones are proteins or amino acid based. (E.g. LH, Epi, ADH) These are usually water soluble and cannot cross cell membrane.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (2) Steroids Some hormones are made from cholesterol. (E.g. aldosterone, estrogen, testosterone) These are all lipid soluble and can cross cell membrane.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Hormones are carried by blood to all tissues. However, not all cells are affected by 1 hormone.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • The cells, that are affected, are “target cells” of a certain hormone.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • These cells have specific receptor proteins in cytoplasm or in cell membrane.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Hormone molecules bind to receptor proteins and trigger a series of changes of these cells.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Mechanisms of water soluble hormones:

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (1) Bind to “plasma membrane receptors” on cell membrane

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (2) Trigger increase of different “second messengers” inside the cell

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • Examples of common second messengers include cAMP, calcium ions, cGMP, etc.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (3) Second messengers activate or inactivate enzymes inside cytoplasm.

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

quotation_candidates.quotation: • (4) Cellular activities are changed!

reference.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)
